title_en: Supreme People's Court Publishes Five Typical Cases of Dishonest Judgment Debtors
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Publishes Five Typical Cases of "Judgment Defaulters"

Case 1:

Zhang Haifeng et al. v. Zhengzhou Longteng Concrete Co., Ltd. — Enforcement Case regarding Dispute over Labor Contracts

(I) Basic Facts

In the enforcement case of Zhang Haifeng and two other migrant workers applying for enforcement against Zhengzhou Longteng Concrete Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhengzhou Longteng Company) regarding a dispute over labor contracts, the Xingyang People's Court of Henan Province ordered Zhengzhou Longteng Company to pay Zhang Haifeng and the other two workers RMB 220,000 in wages and interest.

As Zhengzhou Longteng Company failed to perform the obligations determined by the effective judgment, Zhang Haifeng and the other two workers applied to the Xingyang People's Court for compulsory enforcement. After multiple inquiries, the enforcement court found that all bank accounts of Zhengzhou Longteng Company had no deposits; it also found that the business premises and machinery equipment of Zhengzhou Longteng Company were leased from others and could not be subject to compulsory enforcement. Subsequently, the enforcement court summoned the legal representative of Zhengzhou Longteng Company multiple times, who stated that the company was experiencing operational difficulties and was unable to pay wages, and the case was once at a standstill. Investigation by the enforcement court revealed that the company was still operating normally, but after various compulsory enforcement measures had achieved no significant results, the enforcement court reported the case level by level to the Henan High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Henan High Court). The Enforcement Bureau of Henan High Court decided to list it as a judgment defaulter in accordance with the law, and publicly published the information on the official website of Henan High Court, Sina.com, Dahe Daily, Henan Business Daily, and other online and print media. At the same time, it notified relevant departments such as the Construction Commission, Land and Resources Bureau, Housing Management Bureau, Industry and Commerce Bureau, Taxation Bureau, and financial institutions such as banks, imposing restrictions on the company in terms of loan financing, business registration, tax reduction and exemption, land acquisition, real estate, etc., compressing its business development space, imposing credit sanctions, and urging it to perform its legal obligations.

After the list of judgment defaulters was published, Zhengzhou Longteng Company, under the pressure of public opinion and the deterrence of being listed as a judgment defaulter, fearing that it would have no future business, actively cooperated with the court and voluntarily delivered the full amount of the case to the enforcement court. The case involving the wages of migrant workers was successfully concluded, and the applicants for enforcement expressed satisfaction.

(II) Typical Significance

In strict accordance with the relevant provisions of the Several Opinions (Trial) on Establishing a List of Judgment Defaulters of the Henan High People's Court, the enforcement court listed the judgment debtor that had long failed to perform its obligations under effective legal instruments on the list of judgment defaulters, publicly published the information on the internet and in newspapers, and simultaneously notified relevant joint units in the form of announcements, imposing restrictions on the company in terms of loan financing, business registration, tax reduction and exemption, land acquisition, real estate, etc., compressing its business development space, imposing credit sanctions, and urging it to perform its legal obligations.

Case 2:

Zhengzhou Yijian Commercial Concrete Co., Ltd. v. Henan Guojian Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. — Enforcement Case regarding Dispute over Sales Contract

(I) Basic Facts

In the enforcement case of Zhengzhou Yijian Commercial Concrete Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhengzhou Yijian Company) applying for enforcement against Henan Guojian Construction Engineering Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Henan Guojian Company) regarding a dispute over a sales contract, the Huiji District People's Court of Zhengzhou City (hereinafter referred to as Huiji District Court) ordered Henan Guojian Company to pay Zhengzhou Yijian Company RMB 210,013.85 in payment for goods and RMB 12,226 in liquidated damages and other actual expenses.

Henan Guojian Company did not perform its legal obligations in accordance with the content of the judgment, and Zhengzhou Yijian Company applied to the Huiji District Court for compulsory enforcement.

After the case was accepted for enforcement, the Huiji District Court served an enforcement notice and an order to declare property on Henan Guojian Company, requiring it to perform its obligations within three days. Henan Guojian Company did not perform its obligations in accordance with the enforcement notice, nor did it declare its property to the enforcement court. Investigation by the enforcement court revealed that Henan Guojian Company had no bank deposits or other property available for enforcement, but the company was still operating normally. Enforcement personnel went to the office premises of Henan Guojian Company in Jinshui District for on-site enforcement. The parties involved had a dispute and scuffle over issues such as the amount of interest, and the situation briefly got out of control. After patient efforts by the enforcement court, Henan Guojian Company paid part of the case amount, but subsequently failed to appear in court after multiple summonses and changed its office address to evade enforcement.

In May 2013, Henan High Court listed Henan Guojian Company as a judgment defaulter and publicly published the information on the official website of Henan High Court and in relevant online and print media. At the same time, it notified departments such as the Industry and Commerce Bureau and Taxation Bureau, and financial institutions such as banks, imposing restrictions on the company in terms of loan financing and business registration. After Henan Guojian Company was refused by banks when applying for loans, and saw the company's series of dishonest disclosure information in newspapers and on the Internet, under the dual pressure of public opinion and business operations, it voluntarily approached the Huiji District Court and fully performed the outstanding payments. The parties reached a settlement agreement, and the parties who had previously argued and even fought shook hands and reconciled.

(II) Typical Significance

The enforcement court, by publishing the list of judgment defaulters on the Internet and in newspapers, and simultaneously timely forwarding the information to relevant joint units, imposed restrictions on the judgment debtor in terms of loan financing and real estate, which had a significant impact on the production and operation activities of the judgment debtor. The system of the list of judgment defaulters integrates the role of linkage mechanisms, sharing of dishonest information, and other systems, with strong deterrence and influence, playing an active role in case enforcement.

Case 3:

Qingzhou Rural Credit Cooperative v. Qingzhou Huifeng Construction and Installation Co., Ltd. — Enforcement Case regarding Dispute over Financial Loan Contract

(I) Basic Facts

In the case of a dispute over a financial loan contract between Qingzhou Rural Credit Cooperative of Shandong Province (hereinafter referred to as Qingzhou Credit Cooperative) and Qingzhou Huifeng Construction and Installation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Qingzhou Huifeng Company) and three other companies, the Qingzhou People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Qingzhou Court) concluded the case through mediation, under which Qingzhou Huifeng Company assumed joint and several liability for the principal loan of RMB 1,000,000 and interest. Subsequently, as the borrower and guarantors in the case failed to perform their obligations on schedule, Qingzhou Credit Cooperative applied for compulsory enforcement.

After the court accepted the case for enforcement, in addition to serving legal documents such as enforcement notices and orders to declare property to each judgment debtor, it also served a "Letter of Honest Litigation Tips" and a "Letter of Commitment to Honest Litigation" to them. During the enforcement, the court found that Qingzhou Huifeng Company had two other cases in which it was subject to compulsory enforcement due to failure to perform obligations determined by effective legal instruments. During the enforcement of the above three cases, the dishonest acts of the company, such as refusing to declare property, were collected and entered into the Litigation Integrity Information Database of Qingzhou Court, and its dishonesty level was rated as "seriously dishonest."

The enforcement court, based on the fact that Qingzhou Huifeng Company was involved in multiple cases and had not performed its obligations, and had reached the level of "seriously dishonest," disclosed the information to several joint units of the litigation integrity system, including the Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce. The Industry and Commerce Bureau entered this information into the company's electronic file. In August 2012, the company went to the Industry and Commerce Bureau to undergo an equity change, but the Bureau, upon querying the company's electronic file, found that the company had adverse information regarding dishonesty due to failure to perform legal obligations, and informed the company that it could not handle the change for the time being and that it should first go to the court to go through the relevant procedures before the change could be processed.

The company finally took the matter seriously. Subsequently, it conducted a careful investigation of the performance of its cases in recent years and actively performed its obligations in two other cases where it was the direct obligor. Afterwards, the company applied to the Qingzhou Court to request the court to revoke the adverse information record of the company in the Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce. After accepting the application, the Qingzhou Court reviewed it and found that the cases in which the company assumed direct repayment obligations had indeed been performed, but in the case applied by Qingzhou Credit Cooperative, the company assumed joint and several liability, and the principal debtor in that case had not fully performed its legal obligations. Therefore, the joint and several liability of Qingzhou Huifeng Company was not extinguished. The Qingzhou Court informed Qingzhou Huifeng Company of this situation and ordered it to urge the principal debtor to perform its legal obligations as soon as possible; otherwise, its adverse dishonesty record would not be revoked.

(II) Typical Significance

After the enforcement court disclosed the dishonesty information of the judgment debtor, the joint unit, Qingzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce, entered the information. As a result, the company's equity change registration would be restricted, it would be unable to obtain bidding qualifications, and the land and real estate management departments would also suspend the handling of procedures such as property transfer and ownership changes. The judgment debtor in this case was involved in multiple cases and had delayed in performing legal obligations. After the court's litigation integrity system was put into operation, the company recognized the seriousness of the problem, proactively contacted the enforcement court, and timely performed its obligations in the two cases where it was the direct debtor.

Case 4:

Li v. Shanghai Songdong Baiweijia Catering Management Co., Ltd. — Enforcement Case regarding Dispute over Sales Contract

(I) Basic Facts

In the case of a dispute over a sales contract between Li and Shanghai Songdong Baiweijia Catering Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Baiweijia Catering Company), the Songjiang District People's Court of Shanghai (hereinafter referred to as Songjiang District Court) ordered Baiweijia Catering Company to pay Li RMB 90,100 for the goods.

After the judgment took effect, Baiweijia Catering Company did not perform the obligations determined by the effective judgment, and Li applied to the Songjiang District Court for compulsory enforcement. The enforcement court served an enforcement notice to Baiweijia Catering Company. The legal representative of the company, Hao, appeared in court and claimed that the company was facing operational difficulties and requested the court to stay enforcement. The enforcement court investigated the property status of Baiweijia Catering Company through the Shanghai Court Assistance Enforcement Network and found no valuable leads on property. However, during an on-site visit, the enforcement court found that the company was full of guests and business was booming. The judge randomly interviewed several guests, who all stated that they had purchased group packages online, which were affordable and of good quality. The enforcement court then sealed the company's account books and conducted a deeper investigation, discovering that the catering company was quite famous in Songjiang District of Shanghai, and its largest business volume came from online group purchases, accounting for about 80% of its total business.

To urge Baiweijia Catering Company to perform its obligations, taking into account its business characteristics, and in accordance with the provision of Article 255 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China that information on a judgment debtor's failure to perform obligations may be publicized through the media, the enforcement court lawfully exposed its dishonest conduct of failing to perform the court judgment on the Shanghai Court Internet "Sunshine Enforcement" platform, in the Songjiang Daily of Songjiang District, Shanghai, and other media, and posted announcements of its failure to perform the effective judgment in prominent locations of its several chain stores, so that its target customers—Internet users—would be informed of its dishonest conduct. At first, Baiweijia Catering Company did not care about the enforcement court's exposure of its dishonest conduct in failing to perform its obligations. However, within less than half a month thereafter, the company called the enforcement court multiple times, stating that it recognized the mistake of failing to perform its obligations, but it was indeed difficult to pay the full amount of the debt at that time, and it would strive to negotiate a repayment plan with the applicant for enforcement, Li, and requested the removal of the measures exposing its dishonest conduct. According to the investigation, since the enforcement court exposed Baiweijia Catering Company's failure to perform the court judgment through the Internet, newspapers, announcements, and other means, the news spread rapidly, causing a direct decline in the company's business volume. Regarding Baiweijia Catering Company's request to remove the measures exposing its dishonest conduct, the enforcement court informed the company that before performing the obligations determined by the judgment, removing the dishonest information had no legal basis and would not be supported. Deterred by the power of exposure of dishonest conduct, Baiweijia Catering Company reached an enforcement settlement agreement with the applicant for enforcement, Li, agreeing on a repayment plan, and paid the full amount to the applicant, Li, through installment performance. The enforcement court also lawfully revoked the exposure measures taken against Baiweijia Catering Company, and the case was successfully concluded.

(II) Typical Significance

The enforcement court, seizing the characteristic that businesses value commercial reputation, exposed its conduct of failing to perform the court judgment through channels such as the Internet, newspapers, and announcements, prompting the judgment debtor to perform the obligations determined by the effective judgment through reaching an enforcement settlement agreement with the applicant for enforcement, thereby successfully concluding the case.

Case 5:

Enforcement Case Involving More Than 40 Contract Disputes of a Construction Company in Zhejiang

(I) Basic Facts

Between 2007 and 2009, a construction company in Zhejiang (the judgment debtor) had more than 40 cases that had not been performed in various courts in Hangzhou, Taizhou, Huzhou, Jinhua, Zhoushan, and other places in Zhejiang Province, involving a total subject matter of more than RMB 26 million. The causes of these cases included disputes over sales contracts, disputes over construction project contracting contracts, disputes over work contracts, disputes over lease contracts, etc.

During the enforcement process, the judgment debtor took a negative attitude and rarely cooperated in the investigation of property, claiming that the debts arising from these disputes should be borne by the project management departments or project managers in various locations, and that the project management departments were financially independent from the company headquarters, and thus the company headquarters should not bear the performance obligations. In March 2009, the Enforcement Bureau of the Zhejiang High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Zhejiang High Court) and the Zhejiang Provincial Credit Center established a working mechanism for jointly building and sharing the public joint credit information platform. Zhejiang High Court, through the provincial court enforcement case management system, extracted information on all cases in courts at all levels in the province that had not been actually concluded for more than three months, including the name of the judgment debtor (name of the entity, name of the legal representative), ID number (organization code), address, unperformed amount, case number, enforcement court, and other information, forming separate databases of dishonest information on unperformed effective judgments for individuals and entities, which were submitted to the Provincial Credit Center to be imported into the provincial joint public credit information platform and disclosed on the Credit Zhejiang website for public access and inquiry, and applied in areas such as finance, bidding, and government supervision, to promote the formation of a credit joint prevention and punishment mechanism. The above more than 40 cases of the construction company were all included in the publication, forming more than 40 dishonest records.

According to the relevant provisions of Zhejiang Province on the application of corporate credit reports in the bidding for key construction projects, construction enterprises participating in bidding for key projects must provide corporate credit reports issued by credit rating agencies. If the credit rating does not meet certain conditions, the bidding qualification will be cancelled. Under this provision, if there are two or more dishonest records on the Credit Zhejiang website, the company's credit rating will be downgraded, and it will lose its bidding qualification.

After the enforcement dishonest information was published, the judgment debtor was severely affected in terms of construction enterprise qualification evaluation and project bidding. To improve its credit situation, starting from February 2010, the judgment debtor proactively approached various enforcement courts to seek performance methods. By urging the heads of project departments to actively raise funds to perform obligations and by having the company headquarters allocate funds to cover the balance, the company fully performed all debts by the end of the year. Moreover, the company also learned from this experience, took measures to strengthen risk control, and achieved good results in the gradual decrease of litigation disputes year by year.

(II) Typical Significance

The court, by jointly building and sharing the public joint credit information platform with the credit center, formed a database of dishonest information, which was disclosed on the Internet for public access and inquiry. In this case, the judgment debtor, due to the publication of its dishonest information, had a low credit rating and was severely affected in terms of construction enterprise qualification evaluation and project bidding. To improve its credit status, the judgment debtor voluntarily performed its obligation to pay off debts.
